roadmap_title: Algorand Post-Quantum Cryptography Roadmap
coverage_notes: Algorand Foundation roadmap: native post-quantum accounts targeted for Q3 2026, native Falcon-512 support and multi-cryptography multisig support by end of 2026, broad quantum resilience targeted by 2027. Hybrid model uses both Ed25519 and Falcon signatures for consensus messages during transition; hybrid accounts merge ECC- and lattice-based keys. Algorithms: Falcon-512, Falcon-1024, FN-DSA, ML-DSA. roadmap_title: European Space Agency E2EQSS Post-Quantum Satellite Security
coverage_notes: ESA's E2EQSS project delivers end-to-end quantum-safe security for satellite data links, combining PQC, PKI, QRNG, and CCSDS satellite protocols across two configurations: low-rate (<5Mbps, UHF/S/X-band monitoring & control) and high-rate (<10Gbps, X/K/optical payload data). Status as of Apr 23 2025: SRR complete, PDR in progress, CDR planned for Phase 2, QR as the final milestone. Partners: VisionSpace Technologies (Germany), Ateleris and ID Quantique (Switzerland), Fachhochschule Nordschweiz (Switzerland).

roadmap_title: Gopher Security 2026 Post-Quantum AI Infrastructure Roadmap
coverage_notes: Gopher MCP (on-demand MCP servers/gateways for AI infrastructure) plans ML-KEM (key encapsulation) and ML-DSA (signatures) adoption via a 3-phase strategy: inventory/assessment, implementing PQC primitives, then securing the 'agentic loop' with zero-trust encryption. roadmap_title: GlobalFoundries Post-Quantum Cryptography Partnership with SEALSQ

roadmap_title: 01 Quantum Post-Quantum Cryptography Partnership
coverage_notes: 01 Quantum entered a PQC Engineering Partnership Agreement (announced Jun 10 2026) with a Canadian IT consulting/systems-integration firm to deliver its IronCAP (patented, US #11,271,715 and #11,669,833) PQC technology into public- and private-sector projects in Canada, covering digital assets, AI systems, email security, and enterprise infrastructure. roadmap_title: Quantum Knight Post-Quantum Cryptography for Federal Agencies
coverage_notes: Chugach Government Solutions (CGS) entered a reseller agreement (announced May 13 2026) with Quantum Knight to deliver its CLEAR encryption system (supports Kyber/ML-KEM and Dilithium/ML-DSA, up to 10,240-bit strength, <500KB footprint, with Hyperkey biometric/MFA) to US federal defense, intelligence, healthcare, and civilian agencies. CLEAR secured FDA authorization for medical/digital-infrastructure use in Apr 2025.

roadmap_title: KT Post-Quantum Cryptography and QKD at Quantum Korea 2026
coverage_notes: KT showcased PQC + quantum key distribution (QKD) at Quantum Korea 2026 (Jul 2-4, Seoul): wired QKD at ~300 kbps, wireless QKD demonstrated over 4.8 km near Daejeon (goal: extend beyond 10 km), in-house QKD equipment tech-transferred to a domestic manufacturer. Deployments include a hybrid quantum security network with Shinhan Bank, AI medical data encryption at the National Cancer Center, and a Seoul-Busan quantum cryptography link, spanning public sector, financial services, and defense.

roadmap_title: OneSpan Quantum-Resistant Authentication Suite Server SDK
coverage_notes: OneSpan's 'quantum-resistant' claim for Authentication Suite Server SDK is AES-256 (256-bit keys) for encrypting DPX-files/BLOBs, reasoned via Grover's-algorithm key-search cost — NOT a NIST-standardized PQC algorithm (no ML-KEM/ML-DSA/SLH-DSA/Kyber/Dilithium mentioned). References NIST/NCSC on Grover's algorithm's practical limits but does not adopt post-quantum primitives.

roadmap_title: Sigstore Post-Quantum Cryptography Roadmap
coverage_notes: Sigstore is prioritizing ML-DSA (FIPS 204) over SLH-DSA for its smaller signature size. Phased plan: Go 1.25 (Aug 2025) added SLH-DSA support, Go 1.26 (earliest Feb 2026) targets ML-DSA; client-side experimentation first (PQCA keys via sigstore-go), service-level crypto-agility (Fulcio/Rekor/timestamp authority) led by Trail of Bits comes later, with the public instance waiting on a vetted ML-DSA implementation in Go's standard crypto package. Notes NSA CNSSP 15 mandates CNSA 2.0 algorithms 2027-2031. Open questions remain on verification-material transition and hybrid-algorithm policy.

roadmap_title: Quantum Brilliance Post-Quantum Certified Randomness Partnership
coverage_notes: Quantum Brilliance, CyberSeQ, and LuxProvide signed a letter of intent (Oct 1 2025) to integrate quantum-derived randomness into PQC algorithms. Quantum Brilliance supplies nondeterministic random numbers from a room-temperature virtual QPU; CyberSeQ incorporates 32-byte quantum-derived blocks into PQC algorithms and assesses entropy/certifiability; LuxProvide's MeluXina supercomputer validates the integrated systems. Targets financial services and data-security sectors seeking NIST/BSI/ENISA/ANSSI-aligned certified randomness. No concrete development timeline given beyond the LOI announcement.

roadmap_title: Quantum eMotion QRNG and Quantum-Safe Security
coverage_notes: Quantum eMotion combines electron-based QRNG (1.8 Gbps entropy) with NIST-aligned PQC. Software: Sentry-Q (quantum-safe comms, deployed Dec 2024), eFlux-Q (cloud entropy distribution), eCrypto-Q (QRNG+PQC dev SDK), eHot-Q (crypto-wallet engine; Qastle wallet launched Oct 2025 with Krown), eShield-Q (AI/cloud runtime security). Hardware (in development): eCore-Q, eCMOS-Q, eSOC-Q (with JMEM Tek), eVault-Q, eCold-Q. Milestones: 65nm CMOS design finalized + TSMC manufacturing started May 2025; IBM collaboration validation study completed Jun 2025.

roadmap_title: Palo Alto Networks Post-Quantum Migration Planning
OpenSSL Corporation Post-Quantum Readiness
coverage_notes: OpenSSL has implemented all three NIST PQC standards: ML-KEM (FIPS 203), ML-DSA (FIPS 204), SLH-DSA (FIPS 205). X25519MLKEM768 hybrid key exchange is the TLS 1.3 default. Cites EU roadmap (2030 high-risk systems, 2035 completion) and US CNSA 2.0 (2030 deadline for national-security systems) as external milestones. OpenSSL 3.5 LTS supported through April 2030, with extended fixes available via commercial contracts.

Roadmap phases: short-term commercialization of a "PQC standard chip", mid-term custom QASIC/security-IP solutions, long-term chiplet-based Hardware Security Modules (CHSMs) and Post-Quantum HSMs. First prototype targeted for 2026. roadmap_title: Migration to quantum-resistant cryptography - Ericsson
